citation: Smith, Carl. 'The O'Leary Legend' (essay and galleries) and the O'Leary Legend Library: '“Kate the barn is afire”' (Catherine O'Leary's testimony before the Board of Police and Fire Commissioners, November 1871) and 'The Official Report'. The Great Chicago Fire and the Web of Memory. Chicago History Museum and Northwestern University, 2011.
author: Chicago History Museum and Northwestern University (Carl Smith, principal author); the testimony is the Board's 1871 transcript
describes_date: 1871-10-08 and the inquiry of November-December 1871; the legend to 1997
repository: Chicago History Museum and Northwestern University
locator: The essay at https://greatchicagofire.org/oleary-legend/ and its galleries 'A Star is Born' and the next one, on the legend in the twentieth century; Catherine O'Leary's testimony at https://greatchicagofire.org/oleary-legend-library/%e2%80%9ckate-barn-afire%e2%80%9d/, by question and answer.
rights_note: The testimony of 1871 is public record; the site's transcription, essay and images are (c) 2011 Chicago Historical Society and Northwestern University. Cited for its words in text only; nothing is derived from its images.
access_notes: Read 2026-11-19 (T-3692) on the live pages named in the locator.
note: The museum's transcription of Catherine O'Leary's testimony (the inquiry opened 23 November 1871; she was heard on its second day) is the only verbatim inquiry testimony read for these jaunts; the testimony of Sullivan, Regan and the McLaughlins is read as A. T. Andreas condensed it (andreas_1885_v2). The essay dates Michael Ahern's admission to the fortieth anniversary of the fire, in the Tribune; other modern accounts give 1893.
what_it_supplies: Catherine O'Leary's own words to the Board: in bed, 'Kate the barn is afire', the party, the shavings, the cows
the double cottage, the five children, the McLaughlins in front, the cows, calf and horse
the legend's growth, Michael Ahern's boast, the Bales and meteor theories, the 1971 and 1997 exonerations
what_it_does_not_supply: a cause of the fire: it says it is highly unlikely ever to be known
